quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Which types of drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on this road. In bad weather or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no vehicle from either direction can cross it to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: On a freeway, you realize you missed your turn or exit. You should:

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
Stop and back up.
Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving until you reach the next turn, exit, or other location where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway or shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: The most common color of warning signs is:

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to unexpected conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you wish to turn but you are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn then.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn then.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane there.

questions.question: If a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light signals.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other traffic. Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you, within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: It is permissible to drive a motor vehicle on the left of a highway's centerline:

options.text: When overtaking and passing another vehicle, if passing is permitted.
When you have 500 feet of clear road ahead and to the rear.
When the shoulder of the road is rough and the ditch is deep.
Any time the road is clear of vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When overtaking and passing another vehicle, if passing is permitted.
questions.explanation: You may cross the centerline only when passing another vehicle, if it is legal to pass in that area. Never pass over a solid yellow line or in a no passing zone.

questions.question: What can you do to prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before you brake.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop. When stopping, release the gas to slow down first. Then press the brake pedal with steady pressure. This activates your brake lights and stops your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that road work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them to pass other vehicles if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A cyclist is ahead of you. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign to pass.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or when there are multiple cyclists. Honking can startle cyclists and cause a crash.

questions.question: Is checking your blind spot by turning your head a good driving habit?

options.text: No, it is a bad habit.
Yes, it is a good habit.
No, it is unnecessary.
No, mirrors are enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot before changing lanes, pulling away from the curb, or merging. Look over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?

options.text: The side with lighter traffic.
The same side traffic is moving.
The side facing oncoming traffic.
The side with heavier traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, your reactions slow down. You also feel more confident and make more errors.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away immediately.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them wrong can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a short break every two hours on long trips. If you get drowsy, pull over safely and nap or find a place to sleep for the night.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when it is raining.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians cross here. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of road deaths in Montana?

options.text: Poor roads.
Bad weather.
Drunk drivers.
Speeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drunk drivers.
questions.explanation: Drunk driving causes over 23,000 deaths yearly nationwide. In Montana, half of all traffic deaths and over 2,100 injuries are caused by alcohol. Drunk drivers are the top cause of road deaths in Montana.

questions.question: When should you honk your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn as a warning when another driver or pedestrian may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so poorly they seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so poorly they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, playing music, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to road dangers.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: During a blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off to the side of the road.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?

options.text: An area you cannot see without moving your head.
The area directly behind your vehicle.
An area you see in your rearview mirror.
An area you see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area you cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without moving your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the new speed zone.
Reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A "Reduced speed" sign tells you to slow down. The new speed limit begins at the sign.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge smoothly with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over and make room.
Turn on your high beam headlights so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road's main travel area.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the main travel area. Both drivers need enough space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Winding road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is not allowed. This sign means U-turns are not permitted in this location.
